parsed.explanation: Universal-exposure state measures dominate: passports barred from reflecting lived sex (X markers ended, SCOTUS-backed), visa officers told to refuse on sex-discrepancy doubt with possible lifetime fraud findings, foreign governments issuing travel advisories. Facility bans reach ~21 states (4 criminalising in some circumstances), with a documented trespass arrest and men's-ward placement. Custody exposure is severe — conversion-therapy-style prison policy and immigration-detention abuse — plus state threat-framing ('radically pro-transgender'). Against this: no national trans criminalisation, no sodomy law, hate-crime and employment protections, functioning courts enjoining several orders, and half the states unmapped for bans. Litigation offsets but has not reversed the document regime, placing this in Elevated Risk despite institutional recourse.
